title: The Signal
logline: A lighthouse keeper and a stranded radio engineer pick up a transmission from a ship that sank forty years ago. What they choose to answer decides who gets to leave the island.
style_bible: Anamorphic 35mm, 2.39:1, coastal fog, sodium-vapour practicals, deep teal shadows and warm amber interiors, handheld with slow drift, film grain.

wrenn.name: Ilse Wrenn
wrenn.secret: She was the radio operator who failed to answer the original distress call in 1984.
wrenn.appearance: A woman in her late fifties. Short wavy iron-grey hair, cut practical and wind-blown. Gaunt weathered face with deep lines around the eyes and mouth, sun-and-salt worn skin. Lean wiry build, slightly stooped shoulders.
wrenn.costume: A faded TAN-KHAKI canvas coverall (one-piece boiler suit, colour like wet sand), sleeves rolled to the forearm, brass buttons, dark oil stains at the thighs. A charcoal-grey wool undershirt visible at the open collar. Scuffed DARK BROWN leather lace-up work boots. No hat, no jewellery, no glasses.

okonjo.name: Daniel Okonjo
okonjo.role: Radio engineer, early 30s, stranded by the storm
okonjo.secret: He came to the island deliberately; his father was aboard the lost ship.
okonjo.appearance: A Black man in his early thirties. Close-cropped black hair, short neat beard, high cheekbones, deep brown skin. Slim athletic build, average height.
okonjo.costume: An OLIVE-GREEN short-sleeved utility shirt with two buttoned chest pockets, worn over a black t-shirt. OLIVE-GREEN cargo trousers with thigh pockets. TAN-BROWN leather hiking boots with dark laces. A scuffed dark grey hard-shell RADIO EQUIPMENT CASE with metal latches, carried by hand or strapped across the chest.

voice.name: The Voice on 2182
voice.role: Transmission from the MV Kestrel, lost 1984
voice.secret: It is repeating a conversation that has not happened yet.
voice.appearance: No physical form. Never appears on screen.

world_facts: The island is Skarnholm, nine miles offshore, reachable only by supply boat.
The storm has cut the causeway and the boat is not due for four days.
The lighthouse still carries a working 2182 kHz maritime distress set.
The MV Kestrel went down in 1984 with eleven aboard and was never found.

flags_declared.answered_the_hail: Wrenn or Okonjo transmitted a reply on 2182 kHz.
flags_declared.wrenn_confessed_1984: Wrenn admitted she was on duty the night the Kestrel went down.
flags_declared.okonjo_revealed_father: Okonjo admitted his father was aboard the Kestrel.
flags_declared.logbook_burned: The 1984 logbook was destroyed rather than read.
flags_declared.coordinates_written: The coordinates spoken by the Voice were written down and kept.
flags_declared.lamp_left_dark: The lighthouse lamp was left unlit for a full night.
flags_declared.trusted_the_voice: They followed an instruction given by the Voice.
flags_declared.stayed_silent: They heard the hail and deliberately did not reply.

chapters.title: Nine Miles Offshore
chapters.premise: A storm strands Okonjo at the lighthouse. Something answers on a dead frequency.

beats.premise: Okonjo washes up at the lighthouse door in the storm; Wrenn does not want him inside.
beats.exit_conditions: Okonjo is inside and the two have taken each other's measure.
beats.branch_axis: Does Wrenn extend hospitality or interrogate him?

beats.premise: The 2182 set, unplugged for years, crackles with a voice giving the Kestrel's call sign.
beats.exit_conditions: The hail has been heard by both characters and a decision made about replying.
beats.branch_axis: Answer the transmission, or log it and stay silent?

beats.premise: The Voice references a specific page of the 1984 logbook, which is still in the lighthouse.
beats.exit_conditions: The logbook is either read aloud or destroyed.
beats.branch_axis: Read the 1984 page together, or burn the logbook unread?

chapters.title: What The Water Kept
chapters.premise: The Voice starts giving instructions. Following them works, which is the frightening part.

beats.premise: The Voice recites a set of coordinates, twice, then asks whether anyone is writing them down.
beats.exit_conditions: The coordinates are either recorded or deliberately not recorded.
beats.branch_axis: Write down the coordinates, or refuse to give the Voice anything?

beats.premise: The Voice asks for the lamp to be doused for one night. Wrenn has never let the lamp go dark.
beats.exit_conditions: The lamp is doused or kept burning, and the cost is felt.
beats.branch_axis: Obey the Voice and douse the lamp, or keep the light and refuse?

beats.premise: Okonjo's equipment case reveals a 1984 crew manifest with a name circled.
beats.exit_conditions: Okonjo either tells the truth about why he came or lies convincingly.
beats.branch_axis: Okonjo confesses his father was aboard, or invents a reason?

chapters.title: One Berth
chapters.premise: The supply boat is coming early and there is room for one. The Voice already knows which one.

beats.premise: The Voice plays back, word for word, a conversation the two of them have not had yet.
beats.exit_conditions: Both characters understand the transmission is not from the past.
beats.branch_axis: Confront the Voice directly, or cut power to the set?

beats.premise: Consequence beat: whatever was hidden or destroyed earlier comes due. Payoffs land here.
beats.exit_conditions: The earlier choices have visibly cost or saved something.
beats.branch_axis: Face the consequence together, or let one of them carry it alone?

beats.premise: The boat arrives. There is room for one, and the coordinates matter now.
beats.exit_conditions: A final choice is made about who leaves and what is taken off the island.
beats.branch_axis: Who takes the berth, and do the coordinates leave with them?

payoff_contracts.description: If Wrenn confessed, Okonjo can forgive or weaponize it in chapter 3. If she never did, the Voice says it for her.
Burning the logbook destroys the only proof of the 1984 failure, which changes who is believed at the end.
Without the coordinates the wreck is never found; with them, whoever leaves carries the wreck's location.
A dark lamp is why the boat arrives early, and is also how the Voice proves it can be obeyed.
If Okonjo told the truth, Wrenn can choose to give him the berth. If he lied, she cannot.
Having obeyed the Voice once, its final instruction carries weight it would not otherwise have.
Silence does not stop the Voice. It plays back the reply they never sent, word for word, which is how they learn it is not from the past.

shot_budget.note: Provider ceiling is 15s but MEASURED drift forces 4-6s. At 13-14s the model re-stages blocking, relights, changes location and re-ages characters INSIDE one take (verified: night rain threshold -> sunny balcony -> interior across 35s). Short shots hold identity near the conditioning frame. Heads are now 2-3 short shots rather than 1-2 long ones.
